title: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce - Business Studies - Honesty in Business
exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The quality of consistently stating the facts as they are without distortion or deceit in business transactions is known as
questions.explain: **Truthfulness** refers to the quality of being honest, not telling lies, and presenting facts exactly as they are in all business dealings.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is an attribute of a truthful business person?
questions.explain: **Sincerity** (being genuine and free from pretense) is a core attribute of truthfulness. Deceit, favouritism, and arrogance are negative traits.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All the following are attributes of truthfulness EXCEPT
questions.explain: Reliability, transparency, and integrity are all positive attributes associated with being truthful. **Fraudulence** involves deception and dishonesty.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A common psychological or economic factor that causes some traders to lie about the quality of their goods is
options: the desire to pay government taxes
greed to make excessive profit quickly
the need to donate to charity
a strong belief in religious teachings
questions.explain: **Greed to make excessive profit quickly** is a major factor that causes people to lie, such as passing off inferior goods as high-quality ones just to make more money.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A clerical staff member alters the figures in the petty cash book to hide a mistake they made, hoping the manager won't find out. The primary factor causing this lie is
questions.explain: In an office environment, employees often lie or alter records out of a **fear of punishment**, such as being reprimanded or losing their jobs over mistakes.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: What is a major long-term reward for being truthful in business?
options: Building a good reputation and earning customer trust
Driving competitors out of business with fake prices
Getting immediate wealth without any hard work
Avoiding the payment of rent and salaries
questions.explain: Truthfulness brings long-term rewards, the most significant being the establishment of a **good reputation and customer trust**, which eventually leads to loyal patronage.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An organization that is known for its truthfulness and honesty is highly likely to experience
questions.explain: Customers naturally return to businesses they trust. Therefore, an honest business will experience **repeated patronage**, leading to sustainable sales.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A severe consequence of not being truthful to customers about the safety of a product is
options: loss of trust and potential legal actions
questions.explain: Lying about product safety can result in physical harm to consumers, inevitably leading to a **loss of trust, lawsuits, or even criminal prosecution (legal actions)**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When workers in a firm discover that the management constantly tells lies about salary payments, it most often results in
options: an automatic increase in product quality
questions.explain: Internal untruthfulness breaks the trust between employers and employees, leading to resentment, **demotivation, and low productivity** among the workforce.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The principle of conducting business affairs in a just, equitable, and impartial manner without cheating or favouritism is called
questions.explain: **Fair play** means treating everyone (customers, employees, and suppliers) equally, justly, and according to the rules, without resorting to cheating.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios best demonstrates fair play by a business owner?
options: Paying female workers less than male workers for the same job
Using heavily manipulated weighing scales to sell meat
Selling goods at uniform, agreed prices to all customers regardless of status
Giving promotions only to staff members from a specific hometown
questions.explain: **Selling goods at uniform prices** shows impartiality and equity. The other options describe discrimination, nepotism, and cheating, which violate fair play.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An attribute of fair play in business is
questions.explain: **Objectivity** means making decisions based on facts and merit rather than personal feelings or biases, which is a key attribute of fair play.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All the following are attributes of fair play EXCEPT
questions.explain: Equity, impartiality, and justice all reflect fairness. **Bias** refers to a prejudiced or unfair preference for or against someone, making it the opposite of fair play.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An organization that deliberately spreads false rumours about a competitor's product to boost its own sales is guilty of lacking
questions.explain: Spreading false rumours (lies) about competitors is a malicious tactic that clearly violates the ethical principles of both **fair play and truthfulness** in business.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies
